scenes.heading: Adding and subtracting fractions
scenes.sub: Make the pieces the same size first
scenes.say: What is one third plus one quarter? It's not two sevenths! To add or subtract fractions, the pieces have to be the same size. Let's see how.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: 3 twenty-cent coins + 2 fifty-cent coins: change both into cents
scenes.science: 1/3 + 1/4: change both into twelfths, then add
scenes.breaks: Coins change by their value. Fractions change by finding equivalent fractions, and answers may need simplifying.
scenes.say: Three twenty-cent coins and two fifty-cent coins isn't just five coins. You change them into cents first: sixty plus one hundred is one hundred and sixty cents. Fractions are the same. Thirds and quarters are different-sized pieces, so change them both into twelfths before adding.

scenes.heading: Same denominators
scenes.say: When the bottoms are the same, the pieces are the same size. Just add or subtract the tops and keep the bottom. Two sevenths plus three sevenths is five sevenths, not five fourteenths.
scenes.caption: When the bottoms are the same, the pieces are the same size. Just add or subtract the tops and keep the bottom. 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7, not 5/14.

scenes.heading: Different denominators
steps: Find the LCM of the bottoms
scenes.say: When the bottoms are different, find the lowest common multiple of the bottoms. Make equivalent fractions with that denominator. Add or subtract the tops. Then simplify.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Work out 5/6 − 3/8.
scenes.say: Five sixths take away three eighths. The lowest common multiple of six and eight is twenty-four. Five sixths is twenty twenty-fourths, and three eighths is nine twenty-fourths. Twenty minus nine is eleven, so the answer is eleven twenty-fourths.
scenes.caption: 5/6 − 3/8. The LCM of 6 and 8 is 24. 5/6 = 20/24 and 3/8 = 9/24. 20 − 9 = 11, so the answer is 11/24.

scenes.heading: Mixed numbers
scenes.question: Work out 3¼ − 1⅔.
scenes.say: For mixed numbers, changing to improper fractions always works. Three and a quarter is thirteen quarters, and one and two thirds is five thirds. In twelfths, that's thirty-nine twelfths minus twenty twelfths, which is nineteen twelfths, or one and seven twelfths.
scenes.caption: For mixed numbers, changing to improper fractions always works. 3¼ = 13/4 and 1⅔ = 5/3. In twelfths: 39/12 − 20/12 = 19/12 = 1 7/12.

scenes.heading: Watch out
scenes.say: The big mistake is adding the bottoms. One third plus one quarter can't be two sevenths, because two sevenths is smaller than one third! A quick sense check catches it.
scenes.caption: The big mistake is adding the bottoms. 1/3 + 1/4 can't be 2/7, because 2/7 is smaller than 1/3! A quick sense check catches it.

points: Only add or subtract same-sized pieces
Add or subtract tops; keep the bottom
Use the LCM for a common denominator
scenes.say: Quick recap. Only add or subtract same-sized pieces. Add or subtract the tops and keep the bottom. Use the lowest common multiple for a common denominator. For mixed numbers, improper fractions always work. Now try the practice questions!
